ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, two congruent right triangles overlap each other. One of the triangles is translated along the direction from point B to C to the position of $\triangle DEF$, where $AB=10$, $DO=4$, and the translation distance is $6$. What is the area of the shaded region?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Given the property of translation, we have $BE=6$, $DE=AB=10$,\\
thus $OE=DE-DO=10-4=6$,\\
therefore, the area of quadrilateral $ODFC$ is equal to the area of trapezoid $ABEO$, which is $\frac{1}{2}\times(AB+OE)\times BE =\frac{1}{2}\times(10+6)\times 6=\boxed{48}$.

Image description: In the figure there are two overlapping congruent right triangles. The triangle on the left can be regarded as △ABC, in which AB is the vertical side, BC is on the bottom horizontal line, and AC is the hypotenuse; the translated triangle on the right is △DEF, in which DE is the vertical side, EF is on the same horizontal bottom line, and DF is the hypotenuse. Point O is located at the intersection of the vertical line DE and the slanted line AC, and the shaded part is the quadrilateral ODFC remaining in △DEF after removing the overlapping small triangle △OEC.
Reasoning: The translation direction is from B to C, so the translation distance corresponds to BE=6. Translation preserves length unchanged, so DE=AB=10. It is known that DO=4, so OE=DE-DO=10-4=6. Because △OEC and △ABC are both right triangles and share the same slanted line AC direction, they are similar. Thus OE/AB=EC/BC, namely 6/10=EC/(BE+EC)=EC/(6+EC). Solving gives 10EC=6(6+EC), namely 10EC=36+6EC, so EC=9, and then BC=6+9=15. Translation preserves the base length, so EF=BC=15. Shaded area=area of △DEF-area of △OEC=(1/2)×10×15-(1/2)×6×9=75-27=48.
